subject_matter: Action — the concept space of action in philosophical discourse: intention, reason, the deed, the communicative act, imputation
source: Anscombe, Intention (1957); Davidson, 'Actions, Reasons, and Causes' (1963); Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Nietzsche, On the Genealogy of Morals I §13; Hegel, Philosophy of Right §§115–118; Austin, How to Do Things with Words (1962); Habermas, The Theory of Communicative Action (1981); Kant, Metaphysics of Morals 6:227 (Zurechnung); Ricoeur, Oneself as Another (1990)

signature.meaning: the first rationalizes the second (a primary reason shows the action in a favourable light)
the first is what it is under the description the second gives
the first begins the second (natality: action starts a new chain among others)
the first answers for the second (ascription, responsibility)
the first holds independently of the second
